source_caption:
7 years ago today Quentin Tarantino officially released Once Upon a Time in Hollywood, delivering his most affectionate, atmosphere-driven masterpiece. Moving away from his usual explosive plot structures, Tarantino used the lingering summer of 1969 to build a hypnotic time capsule of a changing Los Angeles. Driven by iconic performances from Leonardo DiCaprio as fading western star Rick Dalton, Brad Pitt as unshakeable stuntman Cliff Booth, and Margot Robbie as Sharon Tate, the film treats its setting not just as a backdrop, but as a living character on the brink of an inevitable historical shift.

What makes this chapter of prestige cinema history so enduring is its phenomenal ensemble cast featuring Al Pacino, Margaret Qualley, Austin Butler, Dakota Fanning, Timothy Olyphant, Emile Hirsch, Mike Moh, and Kurt Russell. By blending real-world history with cinematic fantasy, Tarantino crafts a slow-burn tension that culminates in one of the most cathartic, wildly entertaining climaxes in modern film.

source_details.synopsis: Once Upon a Time... in Hollywood is a 2019 comedy-drama film written and directed by Quentin Tarantino, who produced it with David Heyman and Shannon McIntosh. Produced by Columbia Pictures in association with Bona Film Group, Heyday Films, and Visiona Romantica, and distributed by Sony Pictures Releasing, it is a co-production between the United States, United Kingdom, and China. It features an ensemble cast led by Leonardo DiCaprio as Rick Dalton, an aging Western hero; Brad Pitt as his stunt double Cliff Booth; and Margot Robbie as actress Sharon Tate, wife of Roman Polanski.
